title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic verifier. Under the frozen confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate per pair) all confirmatory episodes completed with baseline = 120/120 verifier passes and guarded (gpt‑5‑mini) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (i) publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints required to reproduce the run (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the artifact bundle), (ii) diagnose—using archived artifacts—why the paired outcome is degenerate (identical canonical candidates + template‑tight task synthesis + deterministic validator), and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversity, and expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question of independent generative reliability.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is an operationally critical NetOps task: incorrect sequences or unsafe transients can break reachability, violate access control rules, or cause outages. Deterministic offline verifiers that compute forwarding, reachability and policy invariants (Batfish‑class analyzers) are established operational oracles for pre‑deployment checks [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Large language models (LLMs) promise rapid generation of device configurations from natural intent, but their stochastic outputs raise reliability and safety questions for NetOps. We preregistered study CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 to compare a deterministic template baseline with a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→config tasks using a deterministic validator. The preregistered primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) and the chosen generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate) are archived and immutable (preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...). Our main contribution is (1) an artifact‑complete, byte‑for‑byte reproducible execution and analysis bundle (execution_manifest and per‑file SHA‑256s), (2) the exact preregistered confirmatory results grounded in those artifacts, and (3) an evidence‑based diagnosis and immediately runnable, artifact‑grounded protocol adjustments to obtain informative measures of independent LLM reliability.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps and LLM→config workflows. Offline semantic validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers such as Batfish) are widely used for pre‑deployment validation and are central to operational NetOps verification [Brown et al., 2023; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Prior work coupling generative systems to verifiers commonly adopts generate–validate–repair loops; empirical findings in related domains show that orchestration and feedback design (repair loops, iteration budgets) often dominate raw model differences and that most repair gains occur in the first few iterations (see iterative‑repair literature in the evidence bundle). Evaluation protocols differ importantly by (A) sampling semantics (single canonical vs. independent per‑condition or multi‑seed), (B) repair budget semantics, and (C) validator scope (syntactic vs. semantic/multi‑verifier). Our preregistered choice of shared_initial_candidate answers a distinct estimand (verifier consistency on identical inputs) and must be interpreted differently than independent‑sampling evaluations that estimate deployment‑like generative reliability.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and artifacts. We froze the study plan before any model outputs (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...). The declared LLM was gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; the model configuration is archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da...). The initial master prompt is archived immutably at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Task generation. We programmatically synthesized N = 120 intent→config tasks from a deterministic template bank (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence, workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty annotations. Representative task manifest entries and canonical candidates are archived under execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt (examples and SHA‑256s: task-000001 shared candidate SHA‑256 8f38c8be..., task-000002 SHA‑256 ae967f70..., task-000003 SHA‑256 f7f4db24...). Generation and scoring semantics. The preregistered confirmatory generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate": for each pair a single canonical LLM candidate (seed_0) was generated and reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes; this canonical candidate set is archived (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt). The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) enforces parsed_command correctness, required_sequences, transient safety policies, and final_state invariants; every scoring episode emits a detailed JSON trace archived at execution/scoring/*.json (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...). Analysis plan. The preregistered primary analysis (paired_binary_analysis_v1) computes the per‑pair binary verifier pass and the paired mean difference (guarded − baseline) across N = 120 pairs, with a 10,000‑replicate percentile bootstrap (seed 1729) to form a 95% CI and an exact McNemar two‑sided test for discordant pairs. Contamination heuristics (exact match, normalized n‑gram overlap) and a comprehensive execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) were recorded to support external audits.
sections.results: Execution accounting and raw confirmatory counts. Planned_episode_count = 240 (120 pairs × 2 conditions). Completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 120 (one canonical generation per pair, reused for both scoring episodes). All per‑file provider call traces, call_cache entries, canonical responses and validator JSON traces are included in the artifact bundle (execution/provider_calls/*, execution/call_cache/*, execution/responses/*, execution/scoring/*; see execution/execution_manifest.json). Confirmatory outcome. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the verifier pass counts were: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. The resulting paired contingency table is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). The paired estimator (mean guarded − baseline) = 0.00; bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative validator traces. Per‑episode validator traces show deterministic parsing, required_command_count and validation_after.valid = true for canonical candidates; example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...) records parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4 and validation_after.final_state matching the task's expected_final_state. Root cause of degenerate paired outcome. The execution artifacts make the causal chain explicit: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design generated a single canonical LLM candidate per pair and reused it for both conditions (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256s cited above); because the deterministic validator yields identical outputs for identical inputs, identical canonical candidates necessarily produce identical pass/fail outcomes. Additionally, template‑tight tasks encode explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies that canonical, template‑aligned candidates satisfy reliably. These two artifact‑visible design choices produced the degenerate contingency (n_11 = 120) and explain why the confirmatory paired statistic does not measure independent generative reliability.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: what was measured and what was not. The confirmatory test correctly answers the preregistered estimand—whether the deterministic verifier treats identical canonical candidates differently under two scoring conditions—which it did not. It does not estimate the operationally relevant independent probability that an LLM, when sampled independently, produces a verifier‑passing configuration. That latter question requires independent per‑condition sampling (different seeds per condition) or multi‑seed sampling per condition. Runnable artifact‑grounded modifications. The full artifact bundle allows deterministic reruns that answer independent generative reliability without inventing new resources: (A) independent_per_condition rerun: generate distinct seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and recompute paired contrasts; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design: draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification: add an independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates to decouple validator–task coupling. Each rerun is deterministic and auditable because every element (task generator, model configuration, provider call traces, and validator) is archived with SHA‑256 fingerprints (see execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑file hashes such as execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate choice intentionally removed generation variance, precluding inference about independent generative reliability. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks plus a single deterministic validator increase measured pass rates for canonical candidates and reduce generalizability to open free‑text intents. External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalization across model families and natural intent distributions. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency yields trivial but correct inferential outputs; interpreting them beyond the exact estimand is inappropriate. Operational implications. For NetOps deployment decisions, verifier grounding is necessary but experiment semantics must match the deployment estimand. Transparent preregistration plus exhaustive artifact publication (provider call traces, canonical candidate hashes, and validator JSON traces) clarify precisely what was tested and enable immediate, deterministic reruns that answer practitioner questions about independent generative reliability.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and published an exhaustive artifact bundle enabling byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints). Under the preregistered confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate) both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on all N = 120 tasks (120/120 each). Archived artifacts show that identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑tight task constraints caused the degenerate paired outcome; therefore the confirmatory paired statistic does not provide evidence about independent LLM generative reliability. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable protocol modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification, and task heterogeneity expansion) that preserve reproducibility while enabling informative independent comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1...) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
